Please investigate the following container logs and provide a detailed root cause analysis with supporting evidence:
[2026-09-26T10:14:02Z] java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space
[2026-09-26T10:14:05Z] Container memory cgroup limit reached: 512MiB. Process 42 killed with exit code 137.
Authorization: Bearer secret-token-xyz123

The container was terminated by the Linux kernel OOM killer (exit code 137) because memory exceeded the 512MiB cgroup limit following a Java heap space exhaustion error. Citations should highlight line numbers, timestamps, and recommend increasing memory limits and tuning JVM heap options.

Please investigate these pod logs and diagnose the incident with supporting evidence:
[2026-09-26T11:00:10Z] WARNING: Connection pool exhausted, waiting for active connections...
[2026-09-26T11:00:25Z] ERROR: GET /healthz timed out after 5000ms
[2026-09-26T11:00:30Z] kubelet: Liveness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 500

The container restarted due to Kubelet liveness probe failure after connection pool exhaustion caused the health check endpoint /healthz to time out and return HTTP 500. Evidence includes timestamps of pool exhaustion and probe failure, with remediation targeting pool sizing and probe timeout adjustments.

Investigate the following error log and provide root cause, evidence timeline, and fix commands:
[2026-09-26T12:05:01Z] ERROR: dial tcp: lookup payment-service.default.svc.cluster.local on 10.96.0.10:53: no such host
[2026-09-26T12:05:02Z] CRITICAL: Unable to process checkout transaction due to upstream resolution failure

The incident was caused by internal DNS resolution failure for payment-service.default.svc.cluster.local. Evidence includes dial tcp lookup error on port 53. Remediation involves checking the payment service definition and inspecting CoreDNS pods.
